buy_title: If you buy one thing for your winter trunk, buy this
buy_total: The button is a paid link: as an Amazon Associate we earn from qualifying purchases, and it never changes what you pay. Prices in this guide come from other US retailers and review sites, with dates; the button shows today's price.

cards.name: NOCO Boost Plus GB40 jump starter (1000 A, lithium)
cards.badge: Our first pick · the one item that changes your day
cards.price: About $100 (a review-site page listed $99.95 against a $124.95 list price, June 2026; not confirmed on noco.com)
cards.buy_if: you drive a gas car, crossover or V6 SUV and want to start it yourself when the battery dies in the cold, without waiting for another car.
cards.skip_if: you drive a big V8 truck or a diesel: The Drive (February 2025) rates it to 6.0L gas and 3.0L diesel, and forum owners of larger engines lean on the heavier Clore Jump-N-Carry JNC660.
cards.owners: Forum owners (Tahoe Yukon Forum, 2020) report a GB40 kept in a console that worked; a Garage Journal thread (September 2023) tells of one that swelled after a jump and others that lost capacity. Both agree: charge it on arrival and keep it in the cabin.

buy.pick: The NOCO Boost Plus GB40 (1000 A). Charge it fully the day it arrives, then top it up every month or two.
buy.check: Buy from noco.com or a big-box store so the 1-year limited warranty and returns are clean, and check the listing says NOCO GB40, not an unbranded 'peak amp' look-alike. The US Consumer Product Safety Commission warned about another brand of lithium jump starters in September 2026 after 16 fire reports.

cards.name: Hopkins SubZero 26 in snow brush and ice scraper
cards.badge: Essential · cheapest fix on the list
cards.price: About $25–$28 (SubZero Quick Lock broom, $27.99 at Tractor Supply per Bob Vila, January 2026; a Walmart listing of a 26 in SubZero showed $24.94, snippet, undated)
cards.buy_if: you park outside. Family Handyman named a SubZero 26 in combo its top pick in a Minnesota test (updated November 2024).
cards.skip_if: you drive a tall SUV or truck and need 48 in or more of reach; owners say large brooms with a foam grip can spin loose in the cold.
cards.owners: A S2000 forum owner says a Hopkins SubZero lasted fifteen winters before snapping; buyers at other stores report shedding bristles and cracked scrapers on cheap telescoping models.

cards.name: Suncast Telescoping Auto Shovel (SCS4506PK)
cards.badge: The folding shovel · check the lock
cards.price: We found no confirmed US price for this model; folding car shovels ran about $15–$30 (Harbor Freight utility shovel $14.99, October 28, 2026; a Walmart Garant car shovel about $25, snippet)
cards.buy_if: you need to dig out a tire or clear the tailpipe, not clear a driveway. Every official list names a shovel; Consumer Reports says a collapsible one will do.
cards.skip_if: you want a tool that survives hard ice: owners say the failures are plastic joints, lock sleeves and single-screw heads, not the blade. Buy a metal blade if you can.
cards.owners: A Home Depot reviewer says the blade flew off within seconds because one screw holds the thin head; another says it works about as well as a metal shovel (snippets, undated). Walmart reviewers of folding shovels most often complain about the lock.

cards.name: MAXSA Escaper Buddy traction mats (2-pack, 20333)
cards.badge: Optional · for icy driveways and hills
cards.price: About $130–$250 for the same 2-pack (Home Depot $129.99, snippet; Tractor Supply $249.99 online, snippet). Check the model number and seller before you pay.
cards.buy_if: you park on a sloped driveway or in an unplowed lot and want a reusable aid that works under a front tire.
cards.skip_if: you stay on plowed roads: coarse sand in a small bag costs about $8 and does most of the job. Skip mats for a heavy truck, or in deep powder, where owners say they shoot out from under the tire.
cards.owners: Reports we read (Home Depot reviewer, undated snippet) include a mat that shot out from under the tire; critics of the brand note a 90-day warranty. The Drive (2023) and AutoGuide (2022) named it but did not test in snow.

cards.name: Black Diamond Astro 300 headlamp (AAA)
cards.badge: Keep in the cabin · uses cold-proof batteries
cards.price: We found no confirmed price for the Astro 300; Black Diamond's Spot 400 was about $50 at REI and Harbor Freight's Braun 500-lumen headlamp $12.99 (October 28, 2026)
cards.buy_if: you may change a tire or dig in the dark. Two free hands matter more than lumens.
cards.skip_if: you want a rechargeable: owners report a few durability complaints on the Astro 300-R, and lithium cells fade in the cold. A $13 budget headlamp is fine for a once-a-winter job.
cards.owners: REI shoppers rate the Astro 300 highly (retailer snapshot, undated). ToolGuyd explains that alkaline AAAs sag in the cold and Energizer Ultimate Lithium AAAs are rated to -40°F.

cards.name: Wool blanket plus a SOL Escape Lite bivy
cards.price: About $25–$55 for a wool-blend blanket (Rothco wool blankets, $23.99 on eBay to $53.99 at Rothco's own store, snippets); a foil emergency blanket about $9 (Coleman at Walmart, snippet)
cards.buy_if: you want to stay warm for hours in a stopped car. Field & Stream and Outdoor Life both say wool keeps warming and a foil sheet is for weight and price.
cards.skip_if: you plan to rely on foil alone: Trailspace and REI reviewers describe condensation and a cold, heat-sink feel, and survival writers say it tears.
cards.owners: Blade Forums posters carry both: a space blanket as a ground cloth or wind layer, and wool for warmth. REI shoppers like the SOL bivy but some say it is not truly water resistant.
